title: Young M dwarfs with a BHAC15 radiative core show no TESS CPV dips: 0 seen where the corotation-ratio model predicts 16 in 125 stars of 1-200 Myr, and dust sublimation does not explain this
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips, probably from material near corotation. Earlier work showed that the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio x explains the age decline of the CPV rate, but only for stars with BP-RP 2.4-3.8 and with a free colour term. We tested x for all colours (BP-RP 1.5-4.2) with the released TESS labels, BANYAN Sigma ages, detection efficiencies and BHAC15 radii, and added the BHAC15 radiative-core fraction at each star's group age. Among 855 rapid rotators of 1-200 Myr (P = 0.15-1 d, 77 CPVs), the 125 stars with a radiative core have no CPVs. An x-only model fitted to fully convective stars predicts 15.9 (bootstrap 12.7-19.2; p = 1e-7). At the same x, their rate is below 0.12 times that of fully convective stars (95%). Within the fully convective stars, x alone predicts each colour bin and age class. The early-M stars have 3-4 times higher signal-to-noise; ambiguous labels, a label-free sharpness score and RUWE < 1.4 give the same result. A threshold in the blackbody temperature at corotation (dust sublimation) fits worse than a Teff threshold (twice the log-likelihood difference 10.3) and leaves 7 CPVs above it. A fixed cut at 3450 K (0.36 solar masses) fits as well as radiative-core onset; the preferred model depends on the age scale. In K2, two CPV-like stars of rho Oph and Upper Sco are hotter than 3450 K and are fully convective in BHAC15 at 1-5 Myr, which agrees with a boundary that moves with core onset. The result favours confinement by the strong dipole fields of fully convective stars. Limitations: one automated vetter; non-magnetic models; 26 hot fully convective TESS stars and 2 K2 stars decide between structure and a fixed mass limit; the old-field test has no power and contains two early-M CPVs.

display.caption: CPV fraction of young BANYAN rapid rotators (1-200 Myr, P = 0.15-1 d) versus Gaia BP-RP. Blue: observed (68% Poisson intervals, counts under the axis). Grey: expected from an x-only model fitted to fully convective stars. Bottom: fraction of stars with a BHAC15 radiative core at their group age. No CPVs occur blueward of BP-RP = 2.4, where x alone predicts 17.

Teff and group age of young TESS rapid rotators (grey) and CPVs (blue), with the BHAC15 radiative-core onset (orange; dashed: core mass fraction 0.4) and the best fixed Teff cut (3450 K). Green: K2 CPV-like stars of Upper Sco (plotted at 10 Myr) and rho Oph (1 Myr). All CPVs lie where BHAC15 stars are fully convective.

(a) Fit quality of threshold models in Teff and in corotation temperature T_eq, of the radiative-core model (no free cut) and of the x-only model (lower is better). A dust-sublimation threshold fits poorly. (b) Observed and expected (95% bootstrap) CPV counts in stars with a radiative core for 14 analysis variants.

citations.reason: Uses its CPV labels, periods, Gaia photometry and light-curve scores for all colours (BP-RP > 1.5). Explains why its CPVs are absent among young early-M stars.
Uses its BANYAN Sigma age classes and injection efficiencies for all 29,707 stars.
Uses its stellar-parameter method unchanged. Its x-only model holds for fully convective stars of all colours without a colour term, but fails for stars with a radiative core.
Reuses its transcribed K2 CPV-like labels (k2io.py) for the Upper Sco and rho Oph test.
Its contraction model is the x-only baseline that we test across stellar colour.
Its clump model has a colour term in the clump intensity; we show that the colour dependence comes mostly from the radiative-core boundary.
Its exclusion of cool blackbody dust agrees with our result that a corotation-temperature (dust sublimation) threshold does not set the CPV boundary.
Flare links of CPV hosts; a possible supply route that we discuss.
Long persistence of CPV host status, which agrees with a fixed stellar property such as internal structure.
Rigid corotation of dips, which agrees with magnetic confinement.
BHAC15 evolutionary tracks with radiative-core mass.
